title: Project: A new colleague on Monday

account.text: Create an account for `{{newUser}}` – with a home directory, `/bin/bash` as the shell and a password, so that the account can be logged in to.
account.hint: `useradd` with `-m` and `-s` creates the account, and `passwd` sets the password. Both need `sudo`.

team.text: Create the group `{{teamGroup}}` and add both `{{newUser}}` and yourself to it. `{{newUser}}` must not have sudo rights – not yet.
team.hint: `groupadd` creates the group and `usermod -aG` adds one member at a time. Don't forget the `-a`!

shared.text: Create the shared folder `/srv/{{teamGroup}}`. It should belong to the group `{{teamGroup}}`, and the group should be able to read, write and enter it – everyone else nothing.
shared.hint: `sudo mkdir`, then `chgrp` for the group and `chmod` for the permissions. The digits for *rwx* for the owner and the group and nothing for others are `770`.

try-access.text: Test the account: become `{{newUser}}`, create a file in `/srv/{{teamGroup}}` and then go back to your own account.
try-access.hint: `su - {{newUser}}` with the password you chose, then `touch` and last `exit`.

welcome-pack.text: The reading for the first week, `{{report}}`, is on the USB stick (`/dev/sdb1`). Put a copy in the home directory of `{{newUser}}` – the file should be owned by `{{newUser}}`, not by root – and unmount the stick when you are done.
welcome-pack.hint: Mount the stick on `/mnt/usb` with `sudo mount`. If you copy as `{{newUser}}` (`sudo -u {{newUser}} cp …`), `{{newUser}}` owns the copy. Finish with `sudo umount` – and don't stand in `/mnt/usb` yourself then.

intranet.text: The team's intranet is the service `myserver`. Use `systemctl` to make sure it is running now **and** starts by itself when the computer boots.
intranet.hint: `systemctl is-active` and `is-enabled` show the state. `enable --now` takes care of both at once.

monday.text: Dress rehearsal for Monday morning: restart the computer and then show in the journal that the intranet started by itself on this boot.
monday.hint: `sudo systemctl reboot` restarts. Then `journalctl` with `-u` for the service and `-b` for this boot shows the lines you are looking for.
